title: Utilizing Carbon from Microwave Plasma Gasification for Carbide Reinforcement in CoCrFeNiMn High-Entropy Alloy
content: The CoCrFeNiMn alloy is one of the most thoroughly studied high-entropy alloys owing to its phase composition and promising mechanical properties [1-3]. Motivated by the strength and ductility of the CoCrFeNiMn alloy, the research of high-entropy alloys (HEA) has partially developed into HEA-based metal matrix composites. Designing the HEA-based composites, a general approach commonly used in other metal-matrix composites, including the in-situ strengthening [4, 5] and ceramic particles addition [6-8], is used in the literature. This study focuses on strengthening the CoCrFeNiMn alloy with various carbides prepared from microwave plasma-gasified (MPG) carbon, a waste by-product of polypropylene gasification. Mechanical alloying of MPG carbon and selected metal powders resulted in carbide formation, which was incorporated in the CoCrFeNiMn alloy through mechanical milling. With subsequential spark plasma sintering, a homogeneously strengthened composite with superior mechanical properties was prepared.
